claims.text: Local atomic configurational disorder in HfNbTaTiZr produces a distributed, heterogeneous internal stress field.
The disorder-induced internal stress field moderates dislocation mobility.
The disorder-induced internal stress field moderates elastic softening at elevated temperatures.
Local compositional fluctuations and associated lattice distortions create the proposed heterogeneous internal stress field.
Increasing temperature enhances atomic mobility in HfNbTaTiZr.
Enhanced atomic mobility allows local configurational disorder to relax stress concentrations.
Relaxation or redistribution of disorder-induced stresses modifies dislocation activity.
The proposed mechanism causes elastic softening relative to a more uniformly ordered state.
The proposed mechanism alters thermal expansion relative to a more uniformly ordered state.
The elastic modulus will decrease measurably with increasing temperature relative to its room-temperature value.
Elevated-temperature stress–strain curves will show improved ductility or altered strain-hardening behavior relative to room temperature.
The thermal expansion coefficient will change relative to its room-temperature baseline.
The predicted mechanical and thermal changes are attributable to redistribution of disorder-induced internal stresses.
The proposed response is expected to apply from room temperature to approximately 800°C.
The proposed response is expected to apply through the elastic and early plastic regimes, up to approximately 10% strain.
Nanoprecipitate formation or phase instability at high temperature may contribute to the observed responses.

contradictions.description: The causal claim is framed as a comparison between disordered and more ordered states, but the stated experiment primarily compares elevated-temperature measurements with room-temperature measurements on the same nominal material. Temperature and configurational order are therefore changed or defined inconsistently, and no clearly prepared less-disordered control is specified.
